## 9.6 Number of β-CD dimer linkage isomers

**Analysis of the linkage**

From 9.5, **L is the A,D-diol** of perbenzyl-β-CD: two primary CH₂OH groups located at glucose units 1 and 4 (spacing = 3 units in one direction, 4 units in the other). Because β-CD has C₇ symmetry (chiral, D-sugars only – no mirror), the two positions "A" (unit 1) and "D" (unit 4) are **constitutionally inequivalent** (from A one meets D after 3 units; from D one meets A after 4 units).

**Building the dimer**

Alkylation (t-BuOK / pentenyl bromide), Grubbs I cross-metathesis and H₂/PtO₂ join **one** primary position of one β-CD to **one** primary position of a second β-CD by a saturated —(CH₂)₈— tether (drawn dimer: each CD keeps one free CH₂OH and gains one CH₂O–linker).

**Counting constitutional linkage isomers**

Each of the two β-CD partners uses either its A- or its D-primary OH to bind the tether. Naming the tethered position on CD1 / CD2:

| CD1 | CD2 | Isomer |
|-----|-----|--------|
| A | A | **A–A** |
| A | D (= D–A after C₂ swap of the two identical CDs) | **A–D** |
| D | D | **D–D** |

Since A and D are inequivalent in an A,D-substituted β-CD, the three combinations give three different constitutional isomers; A–D and D–A are identical by the C₂ symmetry that permutes the two β-CD units.

**Answer**

FINAL ANSWER: 3 constitutional linkage isomers (A–A, A–D, D–D).

## 9.9 Number of hexadifferentiated α-CD isomers

**Reasoning**

A hexadifferentiated α-CD carries **six different** functional groups, one on each of the six primary (C6) positions of the six α-D-glucopyranose units. The macrocycle has **C₆ rotational symmetry** (six equivalent rotational positions), but because α-CD is built exclusively from D-glucose it is **chiral** — no mirror symmetry can be applied (a "flip" would invert every stereocentre and is not a symmetry operation of the molecule).

Therefore the number of distinct arrangements is the number of distinguishable necklaces of 6 different beads under cyclic (but not dihedral) symmetry:

N = 6! / 6 = 5! = **120**

FINAL ANSWER: 120 possible arrangements.
